verdict.rationale: Dagster's own asset checks can verify that a tabular asset matches a specified schema, and results surface in the UI with severity levels. That gives first-party detection of schema mismatches, so breakage need not be silent. Nothing in the evidence shows automatic detection of upstream schema drift or a user-chosen propagation policy such as evolve, fail, or quarantine. missing for 10: automatic upstream schema-change detection, configurable propagation/evolution policies (e.g., add columns vs. fail vs. ignore), documentation of how a failed schema check blocks or alters downstream loads, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a data engineer, upstream schema changes are detected and propagated by a policy I choose, instead of silently breaking loads

citations.quote: Verify that a tabular asset adheres to a specified schema
Asset checks are tests that verify specific properties of your data assets, allowing you to execute data quality checks on your data.
Asset check results will appear in the UI and can be customized through the use of metadata and severity levels
